newsitem.title: USA: Rhode Island Gov, Assembly reach budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Rhode Island Gov, Assembly reach budget deal.

text.p: Rhode Island's General Assembly and Gov. Lincoln Almond late Monday announced a $1.84 billion budget accord that will provide a small income tax cut over the next five years.

The income tax rate would be reduced to 25 percent from 27.5 percent over a five year period under the budget which also includes an investment tax credit that will increase to 10 percent from its present 4.0 percent rate for new machinery and equipment, the governor said in a statement.
The budget agreement also includes a research and development tax credit of 22.5 percent.
Other key components of the budget include a $25 million increase in elementary and secondary education and increased funding to higher education by an additional $5 million.

The agreement also includes: a transfer of two cents from the gas tax and one penny added each year thereafter until the full gas tax goes to roads and highways; an increase of $500,000 for the Slater Technology Fund for a total of $2 million; and additional funding of $2 million for programs to help move individuals from welfare to work and full replacement of food stamps cut by federal government.
